memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your offering while I go aside. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet with me. Whatever he reveals to me I will tell you." Then he went off to a barren height. - Num 23:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam leaves Balak beside the altars and goes off alone to a barren height, hoping the Lord will meet him. He says he will report whatever God reveals. There is at least this much truth in Balaam's posture: he knows that any real word must come from God, not from himself.

It is striking that even this compromised man understood that he could not manufacture a message. He had to wait for God to speak. Whatever was tangled in his heart, he grasped that the outcome rested in the hands of the Lord, not in his own cleverness or Balak's silver.

There is a lesson here even from an unlikely source. We cannot force God's hand or generate His word by our own effort. We must come and wait upon Him, ready to receive what He gives rather than what we might prefer. Waiting on God is an act of humility, an admission that He alone holds the truth.

How much better it is to wait on the Lord with a surrendered heart than a scheming one. For those in Christ, we come not to a distant deity we must coax, but to a Father who speaks to us clearly through His Word and His Son (Heb 1:1-2). Wait on Him, and He will not leave you without His voice.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you truly wait on God, or try to generate your own answers?
2. What does it look like to receive God's word rather than demand your own?
3. How does God's willingness to speak in Christ encourage your waiting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to wait on You with a humble and surrendered heart. Help me to receive Your word rather than insist on my own, trusting that You will speak. Amen.
